A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable 24-page versions of Flow-Attentional Graph Neural Networks, including Appendices A–G. Text comparison and rendered-page checks establish matching material except for Equation (15) and the arXiv version/date stamp.

before.justification: v2 reports original PowerGraph classification and Ckt-Bench101 regression experiments in Section 6, plus additional evaluations, attention correlations, and timing measurements in Appendix G.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experimental results in Section 6 and Appendix G.

M1.justification: Section 5.3, Equation (15), changes the specified forward-message aggregation from outgoing neighbors N_out(i) to incoming neighbors N_in(i). This localized correction aligns the formula with the existing forward-pass description; it does not establish that the implementation changed.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same PowerGraph systems, Ckt-Bench101 circuit-property tasks, citation networks Cora/CiteSeer/PubMed, and ogbg-molhiv molecular classification task.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is identical in Tables 1, 2, 5, and 6, including the standard GNNs, DAG baselines, and SAT, GPS, and Exphormer comparisons.

E3.justification: Experimental settings are unchanged, including the 85/5/10 PowerGraph and 80/10/10 Ckt-Bench101 splits, metrics, optimization procedures, training budgets, and Appendix G protocols.

E4.justification: The attention-weight correlation analysis in Appendix G.1 and training/inference efficiency comparisons in Appendix G.4 are identical. No ablation, robustness test, or case study is added or revised.

E5.justification: Both versions retain five-seed mean and standard-deviation reporting in Tables 1 and 5, ten-seed reporting in Tables 2 and 6, and ten-run timing averages in Figures 7–8.

E6.justification: All numerical results and reported findings match, including Tables 1, 2, 5, and 6 and the correlation and timing plots in Figures 6–8. No results are added, removed, or corrected.

T1.justification: Equation (15)'s mathematical definition of the forward aggregate is corrected from N_out(i) to N_in(i), resolving its inconsistency with Equations (9)–(10). The assumptions, expressivity statements, and proofs, including Appendix A, are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about resource-conserving flow attention, enhanced graph discrimination, FlowDAGNN, and improved classification/regression performance.

C2.justification: The explanations of flow attention and the reverse pass, applicability limits beyond flow graphs, Transformer performance/efficiency tradeoffs, and implementation caveat for timing comparisons are unchanged.

D1.justification: The implementation and reproducibility disclosures remain identical, including hyperparameters, dataset details, baseline configurations, GPU information, and the code-availability statement.

R1.justification: The cited works, reference list, related-work discussion, and positioning relative to standard attention, DAG models, and physics-informed approaches are unchanged.

P1.justification: The arXiv margin stamp changes from v2 dated 27 September 2025 to v3 dated 14 November 2025. Prose, terminology, headings, and document organization otherwise remain identical.

P2.justification: Figures 1–8 and Tables 1–6 retain identical displays, captions, and placement. The equation correction introduces no substantive layout revision; pagination remains unchanged.

improvement.justification: v3 corrects the erroneous outgoing-neighbor summation in Equation (15), making the FlowDAGNN formula consistent with its forward-pass description and earlier aggregation equations. This improves mathematical consistency and reduces implementation ambiguity. The benefit is limited: empirical evidence, theoretical claims and proofs, and all appendix content remain unchanged.
